@title CertificateRegistry
 @notice Spec Phase 4 / Level 1 verification, full module (sections
 22-31). Keyed by certificateId (not by hash - a real change from this
 contract's earlier hash-keyed version), so a lookup can compare a
 freshly-recomputed candidate hash against whatever was actually
 registered (spec section 30's "Blockchain Query -> Stored Hash ->
 Compare"), and so a correction never mutates history: registering the
 same certificateId again appends a new, independent version rather
 than overwriting one (spec section 23: "Institutions must NOT be able
 to modify an already finalized Blockchain record. If correction is
 required, create a new version/revocation record"). Every version
 ever written stays readable forever via getCertificateVersion; only
 the latest one is authoritative for verifyCertificate/getCertificate.
 Does NOT store certificate files or personal data (spec section 25) -
 only a hash, a few identifiers, and an IPFS CID pointing at the
 (separately encrypted, see certify-backend's ipfs_service.py) document.
 Access control (spec section 28's "Only authorized institution wallets
 should be able to register their certificates"): a fixed owner address
 (set at deploy time, immutable) maintains an authorized-issuer
 allowlist. Registering and revoking both require msg.sender to be on
 it; verifying and reading are open to anyone, no wallet needed - the
 whole point of an on-chain registry is that anyone can check it.
